intent: Single-variable step from the iteration 8 design: wheel_radius 0.040 to 0.044 m, with sensor_size reverted to 0.012 m (the iteration 9 footprint change hurt slalom finishes). Everything else matches iteration 8, so the Integrator's controller carries over and the effect of the wheel change can be read directly. Expect completion_time to fall by about 0.1 to 0.2 s on the slalom and oval, with completions held at 60/60 and line_loss_events near 1.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that a 0.016 m sensor footprint cut s-bend line loss (0.85 to 0.70) but raised slalom off_track endings (0 to 4 of 20), so sensor blur on sharp bends is worse than the dropouts it removes. Keep 0.012 m. Next iteration, check: (a) whether completion_time falls below 2.2 s on the slalom, which would confirm ground speed is worth more than the turn-rate cost of a larger wheel; (b) whether steering_oscillation rises above 0.30 on the slalom, which would mean the larger wheel has added too much turn rate and kd needs retuning; (c) whether any slalom run goes off_track, which would mean the larger wheel has cost stability; (d) whether line_loss_events stay near 1 per run, which would show that the remaining score gap is in sensing and not speed.
rationale:
Iteration 8 (sensor 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.105 m, wheel_radius 0.04 m, body 0.10 x 0.08 m, mass 0.40 kg) is the best design so far at 939.3. All 60 development trials finished, with progress about 0.996 to 0.998 and rms_error 0.0056 to 0.0099 m. Iteration 9 changed only sensor_size to 0.016 m and scored 902.0. Slalom finishes fell from 20/20 to 16/20, with 4 off_track endings and mean slalom score 821. The wider footprint blurred the signal on the sharpest bends. It did lower s-bend line_loss_events (0.85 to 0.70), but that gain was outweighed by the slalom losses, so I am reverting sensor_size to 0.012 m.

With the geometry fixed at iteration 8, the score terms still open are: line_loss_events (about 1 per run, worth about 105 points at 1 event versus 0 events), completion_time (slalom about 2.26 s, worth about 15 points; oval about 1.85 s, worth about 22 points), and rms_error (about 65 points, already near its ceiling). The most reachable remaining gain is completion time. Iterations 2 to 4 showed that wheel_radius raises ground speed, and runs now finish with margin, so a larger wheel is the next single-variable step. I am raising wheel_radius from 0.040 to 0.044 m and changing nothing else. Expected result: completion_time falls by roughly 0.1 to 0.2 s on the slalom and oval, with 60/60 completions and rms_error held near 0.01 m. Risk: a larger radius raises the turn rate per unit of wheel differential, which could increase steering_oscillation on the slalom (0.26 now) and push slalom off_track endings back up. If that happens, I will return to 0.040 m.
